title: balance.json health block parsed with truncating jint instead of jint_strict — crafted values silently wrap/truncate into valid ranges
evidence:
if hobj, okh := obj["health"].(json.Object); okh {
			b.health.window_ticks = jint(hobj, "window_ticks", -1)
			b.health.exit_margin_pct = jint(hobj, "exit_margin_pct", -1)
			b.health.exit_margin_ms = jint(hobj, "exit_margin_ms", -1)
			b.health.drain_cap_pct_per_tick = jint(hobj, "drain_cap_pct_per_tick", -1)
			b.health.recharge_pct_per_tick = jint(hobj, "recharge_pct_per_tick", -1)
			b.health.win_uptime_pct = jint(hobj, "win_uptime_pct", -1)
			b.health.grace_refill_per_tick = jint(hobj, "grace_refill_per_tick", -1)
			b.health.grace_refill_streak_ticks = jint(hobj, "grace_refill_streak_ticks", -1)
detail: jint (catalog.odin:924-931) does `case json.Integer: return i32(x)` / `case json.Float: return i32(x)` — i64→i32 wrap and decimal truncation. "window_ticks": 4294967497 silently becomes 201; 200.5 becomes 200. packet_types uses jint_strict, which rejects both — the health block doesn't.
recommended_fix: Parse the health block with jint_strict (reject decimals and out-of-i32-range ints) with defaults -1, matching the packet_types bar.

title: No upper bounds on drain severity / drain cap / recharge — crafted catalog empties the meter in one tick, breaking E16 'never instant'
detail: Severity (>=0) and cap (>=1) have no upper bound: a file with drain_cap_pct_per_tick >= 100 makes the first drain tick pass `h.meter_pct <= drain` (100 <= 100) — instant Run_Lost. E16's documented 'never instant / 100/cap ticks' guarantee becomes data-dependent.
recommended_fix: Fail-fast upper bounds at load: health_drain_pct_per_tick and drain_cap_pct_per_tick <= 99 (meter can never empty in one tick), recharge_pct_per_tick bounded likewise.

title: packet_types roster uncapped — crafted catalog drives unbounded health ring allocation and class u16 truncation in grace events
evidence:
entries, oke := obj["entries"].(json.Array)
		if !oke { return {"packet_types.json", "entries", "missing array"} }
		cat.packet_types = make([dynamic]Packet_Type, 0, 8, allocator)
...
	win := u32(cat.balance.health.window_ticks)
	want := n * int(win)
	if win != h.window_ticks || len(h.ring) != want {
		old_len := len(h.ring)
		h.window_ticks = win
		resize(&h.ring, want)
...
					event_emit_health(state, tick, EVENT_TAG_GRACE_STARTED, u16(c))
detail: window_ticks is capped at 10000 but the packet_types roster has no entry cap (crises caps at 255, set-pieces at 65535). Ring = classes x window x 16 B — 100k crafted classes x 10000 = 16 GB from file data; past 65535 classes, u16(c) truncates grace-event class payloads.
recommended_fix: Cap packet_types entries at load (e.g. <= 65535, the class u16 payload byte), mirroring the crises and set-piece roster caps.

title: health_update computes tick % window with no runtime guard — a catalog bypassing catalogs_load (window_ticks = 0) divides by zero
evidence:
win := u64(h.window_ticks)
...
		slot := int(c) * int(h.window_ticks) + int(tick % win)
detail: window_ticks >= 1 is enforced only in catalogs_load; health_update itself never checks. Any run on a hand-built catalog without the health block (tests, harness, future deserialized catalogs) panics on the first tick with demand.
recommended_fix: Guard in health_update/health_ensure: if window_ticks == 0, treat the layer as inert (skip ring/latch) instead of dividing by zero.
